title: Ravya bar Kisi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: In the passage Hyman cites as Yoma 42b (compare [42a:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.42a.3)), Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta and the Rabbis disagree about the weight of the strip of the red heifer, and Rabbi Yirmeyah of Difti said to Ravina: “They do not disagree about the heifer but about the scapegoat.” “And that day Ravya bar Kisi died, and they gave a mnemonic for it: Ravya bar Kisi atones like the scapegoat.” [Rashi on Yoma 42a:3:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Yoma.42a.3.2) explains: on the day they disagreed about it, Ravya bar Kisi died. Hyman reads Rashi as referring to Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta’s time; Hyman’s own plain-sense reading is that Ravya bar Kisi died in Ravina’s time. Hyman finds the same interpretation in Yuchasin. As Hyman quotes it, Ravina relates that Rabbi Yirmeyah of Difta told him the dispute concerned the scapegoat. The quotation gives the mnemonic “Ravya bar Kisi atones” because he died then. Hyman notes that the Gemara has Rabbi Yirmeyah of Difti speaking to Ravina, while he reports that Dikdukei Soferim follows Yuchasin. Hyman takes that reading to answer the objection in Maskil LeEitan.[^4]
In [Chullin 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.20b.4) we find Ravin bar Kisi, and in [Bava Batra 63a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.63a.3) Ravina bar Kisi.

notes.text: Ravya bar Kisi is the one who died in the proposed Ravina-era reading, not Ravina dying in his own days. Maskil LeEitan is the full work title. Hyman’s Rashi interpretation and Yuchasin/Dikdukei Soferim alternatives remain attributed.

The consulted dispute and death mnemonic are at Yoma 42a, while Hyman supplies 42b. The Gemara names Ravya [bar] Kisi. Rashi’s inspected gloss says he died on the disputed day and calls it a sage’s name; it does not explicitly resolve Hyman’s competing era interpretations. Exact Yuchasin and Dikdukei Soferim editions remain uninspected.

The passage that distinguishes the heifer from the scapegoat and then gives the mnemonic is at [Yoma 42a:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.42a.3) in the consulted text. [Chullin 20b:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.20b.4) distinguishes Ravina from his informant Ravin bar Kisi; [Bava Batra 63a:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.63a.3) names Ravina bar Kisi.

The linked Rashi gloss says Ravya died on the day of the dispute. Hyman takes this to refer to Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta’s time, though the gloss does not name the era. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3206&lang=en) uses the report introduced by Ravina and cites Yoma 42a; its Hebrew mnemonic gives דביא. Hyman’s Yuchasin and Dikdukei Soferim readings remain attributed to him.
